block.title: existsb walked whole lists in the λANF build, because orb did not short-circuit
block.p: The libnanofil thread found that regex functions above about 500 blocks took far longer in the λANF build of the backend than in the OCaml one: 9 seconds against 0.6 for a function of 521 blocks. The profile pointed at the validator's evidence_meet, fact_eqb and existsb. The validator itself was not the cause. 81% of the time went to existsb, which never stopped at a match.

Gallina's existsb f (a :: l) is f a || existsb f l. OCaml's extraction makes || its lazy operator, so the call on the rest of the list runs only when f a is false, and it is a tail call. CertiRocq evaluates every argument before a call, so the λANF build called existsb on the rest first, every time, and walked every list to its end, recursing once per element. A membership test that OCaml answers at the first element costs the whole list here.

The fix makes the lowered code skip a call whose result the taken branch never reads. The simplifier of AnfLower.v now inlines a tail call of a small case function such as orb, andb or negb, whose arms only halt. It then moves a call into the one arm of the case after it that reads the call's result. A Gallina function is pure and total, so the call can run on that arm's path alone. In the backend, ten recursive functions become loops, among them existsb and forallb.
The arms must only halt. A first version also inlined case functions whose arms call others. It split the body of merge_steps in two, which used 496 bytes of stack per element instead of 288.

claim.p: On all 53 IR fixtures, for compile, compile-promoted and compile-allocated, the arena build prints the same assembly, stderr and exit status as the OCaml build: 0 of 159 runs differ.

metrics.baseline: the λANF build at d2784c6, compile-allocated

block.p: The function of 521 blocks still takes about five times as long as in the OCaml build. The two builds now do the same work, and the rest of the gap is the cost of each call. The deepest recursion on lvm.ir is now app, which conses after its recursive call, as merge_steps does.
